This model actually had some torque on turns, left turn seems stronger. Also instant unwind. Long seemed pretty good, didn’t find any obvious fails in my 10 mile trip

Comparing everything to OP master model has an implication that master model is supposed to be good? Nevada is rather horrible and dangerous for lat on my Toyota which made me quickly give up on responding to the survey when it asked me to compare to it.

A model being labeled "Master" implies that comma themselves think the model's good enough to for everyone to use. If you don't think the master model is good, then that just makes it easier for you to label. (I also had to stop using Nevada cuz it got pretty bad)
The devs themselves asked for future models to be compared to master since that's what they're really looking at.
You can also skip any question you don't want to answer, no questions are required to submit your response.

Drove for a while. Not a big change but overall feels more smooth and stable than gwm 5, and didn’t notice any regressions.
I've stopped at a FEW stop signs, but still missing a lot. Lat is great, long can use some work on stopping. Highways are solid, but it always is, to be fair

Same, no successful stop signs, but pretty good lat. 
Highway was never an issue, but with enough city / suburb driving, the models would slowly get more comfortable with riding the left line.
No signs of that happening yet with this one, but that takes time to find out.
No lane lines still has it driving in the middle of the road, but on some turns it's where I would be driving.
Overall better than Nevada.
what about red lights?
The stopping distance behind cars is massive. Could build an Amazon warehouse between me and the lead.
I have the opposite. Keep disengaging because it doesn't want to stop creeping up to people
Maybe tall vehicle problem
still cutting corner in turns 😭

Took it on a longer drive today, mix of highway and rural/in town.  Overall like it better than NV and plan to continue on it for now.   Only one stop light as lead, was aggressively slowing to a good point, though didn't get to see  what it'd do as the light turned green before it would have stopped.  All good behavior, saw the green and continued.   Lateral - approx. same torque as NV, perhaps a little more on left turns.   I did note some ratchet-like steering unwind on sharp low-speed turns seen (and not seen) in some other models.   Lane changes are crisp.   Any more and they'd be abrupt/jerky.

I enjoyed gwm6 because of poor feedback from most people, so I have been driving GmW5 since it has been released. Drove about 25 minutes today all city and back roads and I would say this model is a slight improvement on GmW5.  Seems to start 90 degree turns better, still unwinds too late but is noticably better. Only tested lat, probably will be my new daily until the next one comes out. (I already filled out the survey form).
I’ve had an issue with all the later WM versions slowing to 1-2mph for stop lights, then trying to go again when the light is still red. v7 seems to be the same.
This model hugged to the right on the highway for me. Overall I prefer firehose and Nevada. Torque requested was great on this model though. I may use this more for city driving and not highway
This model seems to pass over the right line a lot on the highway
but it does not appear to have the strong left bias that previous gwm models had in my car
